summary: This study demonstrates the use of atomic layer deposited gallium oxide (Ga2O3) for effective passivation of n- and p-type crystalline silicon surfaces. The process uses trimethylgallium (TMGa) and ozone (O3) as precursors, with optimal passivation achieved at a deposition temperature range of 200–250 °C. The passivation results in a surface recombination velocity (SRV) as low as 6.1 cm/s and a minority carrier lifetime of up to 2.5 ms. The activation energy for passivation is approximately 0.5 eV, while the depassivation activation energy is 1.9 eV.
evidence: Effective passivation of n- and p-type crystalline silicon surfaces has been achieved by the application of very thin Ga2O3 films prepared by atomic layer deposition using trimethylgallium (TMGa) and ozone (O3) as the reactants. Surface recombination velocities as low as 6.1 cm/s have been recorded with films less than 4.5 nm thick. The thermal activation energy for passivation of the Si-Ga2O3 interface has been found to be approximately 0.5 eV. Depassivation of the interface was observed for prolonged annealing at increased temperatures. The activation energy for depassivation was measured to be 1.9 eV.
